headline: Referred revised trespass ordinance on appeal hearing timing to full City Council with recommendation for adoption.
summary: The committee reviewed revised changes to the Trespass on City Property ordinance, BCO Sec. 21-45A(F)(3), covering appeal hearing timing. The revised draft lets the Public Safety Committee grant a stay of a trespass if the trespassed person asks and the issuing officer does not show exigent circumstances within one business day. The committee unanimously added a requirement that any time extensions and their rationale be noted in the final decision, and referred the ordinance to the full City Council with a recommendation for adoption.
decisions: Referred the revised trespass ordinance to the full City Council with a recommendation for adoption, unanimously.

decision_titles: Trespass on City Property Appeal Hearing Scheduling Timing Ordinance
plain_text:
Ordinance Committee 
Tuesday, October 13, 2026 
Bushor Conference Room, City Hall 
or Remote via Zoom. Burlington, Vermont 
DRAFT MINUTES 
 
 
Members Present: Councilor Bergman (Chair), Councilor Barlow, Councilor Carpenter 
Staff Present: Kim Sturtevant (Assistant City Attorney), Hayley McClenahan (Assistant City 
Attorney) 
Public Present: Sharon Bushor 
Meeting called to order at 5:34 PM. 
1. Adopt the Agenda 
1.1 Adopt the Agenda 
Motion to Adopt Agenda. 
Motion by Councilor Barlow, Seconded by Councilor Carpenter. 
Final Resolution: Motion Passes 
Yes: Unanimous 
 
2. Adopt Draft Minutes 
2.1 Adopt Draft Minutes from October 2, 2026 
Motion to adopt the draft minutes from October 2, 2026 as drafted. 
Motion by Councilor Barlow, Seconded by Councilor Carpenter. 
Final Resolution: Motion Passes 
Yes: Unanimous 
  
3. Public Forum 
Sharon Bushor: I like the revised draft.  Will the party that requests a time extension and their 
rationale be documented? Would that decision be made at a meeting or internal?  I think the 
rationale for an extension should be part of the public hearing record. 
4.  BCO Sec. 21-45A(F)(3) Trespass on City Property - Appeal Hearing Scheduling Timing 
Councilor Carpenter asked if the Public Safety Committee is a quasi-judicial body that has 
different open meeting law rules. 
Attorney McClenahan responded to Sharon Bushor’s question that the ordinance does not speak 
to that question, but that it has been the practice to include information about extensions in the 
final decision.  She continued that in at least one of the appeal requests that both parties agreed to 
an extension so that the appellant could finish their public records requests.  She then responded
to Councilor Carpenter’s question that the Public Safety Committee’s deliberations are captured 
in the final decision in a similar way to how a court will have a hearing and then release an order 
or decision some time after.  There is no need to warn the Public Safety Committee’s 
deliberations about a hearing and they are often done by email. 
Attorney Sturtevant shared the revised draft ordinance and Attorney McClenahan went through 
the changes since the previous meeting.  This draft ordinance is available in the agenda packet 
on CivicClerk. 
Councilor Bergman asked if it would be difficult to include in ordinance that the final decisions 
always include any rationale for possible extensions. 
Attorney McClenahan said it would be possible, but that it could be too granular for what to 
include in ordinance.  She continued that it is the responsibility of the Public Safety Committee 
to include in their final decision all of the relevant details of the case. 
Councilor Carpenter asked to clarify that if a person is trespassed that they have one day before 
the trespass takes effect.  Attorney McClenahan said no, a trespass takes effect when notice is 
given to the trespassed party.  She said that under the revised ordinance, a stay of the trespass 
could be granted by the Public Safety Committee if the trespassed person asks for a stay and the 
issuing officer does not respond within one business day that there are exigent circumstances.  A 
stay is only in effect until the Public Safety Committee makes their decision after the hearing. 
Motion to approve the revised ordinance change with the addition of a further change to require 
any time extensions and their rationale to be noted in the final decision of the Public Safety 
Committee, and to refer the revised draft ordinance back to the full City Council with a 
recommendation for adoption. 
Motion by Councilor Barlow, Seconded by Councilor Carpenter. 
Final Resolution: Motion Passes 
Yes: Unanimous 
 
5. Any Other Committee Business 
The next Ordinance Committee meeting is October 28th at 4:00PM. 
6. Adjournment 
Motion to adjourn by Councilor Bergman, without objection. 
The meeting was adjourned at 6:06 PM.
